paragraphs: ¹⁶ "Son of man, take one stick and write on it, 'For Judah and the Israelites associated with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and all the house of Israel associated with him.' ¹⁷ Join them together into one stick so they become one in your hand. ¹⁸ When your people ask you, 'Won't you explain to us what you mean by this?' ¹⁹ tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, along with the tribes of Israel associated with him, and join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them one stick, and they will be one in my hand. ²⁰ Hold before their eyes the sticks you have written on.

²¹ Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: I am going to take the Israelites from among the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them back to their own land. ²² I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will rule all of them, and they will never again be two nations or divided into two kingdoms. ²³ They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their detestable practices, or any of their rebellions. I will save them from all the places where they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God. ²⁴ My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my laws and keep my decrees and observe them. ²⁵ They will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, the land where your ancestors lived. They will live there — they, their children, and their children's children — forever. And my servant David will be their prince forever.

²⁶ I will make a covenant of peace with them — an everlasting covenant. I will establish them, multiply them, and set my sanctuary among them forever. ²⁷ My dwelling place will be with them. I will be their God, and they will be my people. ²⁸ Then the nations will know that I the LORD make Israel holy, when my sanctuary stands among them forever.

¹ The word of the LORD came to me: ² "Son of man, turn your face against Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him. ³ Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. ⁴ I will turn you around and put hooks in your jaws, and I will bring you out with your whole army — horses and horsemen, all fully armed, a great company with shields and bucklers, all wielding swords — ⁵ with Persia, Cush, and Put among them, all with shields and helmets.

⁶ Also Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the far north with all its troops — and many other peoples with you. ⁷ Get ready; be prepared, you and all the companies gathered around you, and take command of them. ⁸ After many days you will be summoned. In later years you will come against a land recovered from war, a people gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate. These people have been brought out from the nations, and now all of them are living safely. ⁹ You will advance, coming on like a storm — you and all your troops and many other peoples with you, like a cloud covering the land. ¹⁰ This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day, thoughts will come to your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.

¹¹ You will say, "I will march against a land of unwalled villages; I will attack those who are at peace and living in safety — people with no walls, no bars, no gates — ¹² to plunder and loot, to turn your hand against the resettled ruins and against the people gathered from the nations, who now have cattle and goods and live at the center of the land." ¹³ Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish, with all its young lions, will ask you: "Have you come to plunder? Have you assembled your forces to loot, to make off with silver and gold, to take away cattle and goods, to seize a great spoil?" ¹⁴ Therefore, son of man, prophesy and say to Gog: This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day when my people Israel are living safely, will you not take notice? ¹⁵ You will come from your place in the far north, you and many peoples with you — all of them riding horses, a vast army, a mighty force.

¹⁶ You will advance against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the last days this will happen, and I will bring you against my land so that the nations may know me, when I demonstrate my holiness through you before their eyes, O Gog. ¹⁷ This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you the one I spoke of in earlier times through my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied for years that I would bring you against them? ¹⁸ On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my fierce anger will flare up. ¹⁹ In my zeal and fiery wrath I declare that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel. ²⁰ The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the field, every creature that moves along the ground, and all the people on the face of the earth will tremble at my presence. The mountains will be overturned, the cliffs will crumble, and every wall will fall to the ground.

²¹ I will summon a sword against Gog on all my mountains, declares the Lord GOD. Every man's sword will be turned against his brother. ²² I will punish him with plague and with bloodshed. I will pour down torrents of rain, hailstones, and burning sulfur on him and his troops and on the many nations with him. ²³ In this way I will show my greatness and my holiness, and I will make myself known in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

¹ "Son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. ² I will turn you around and drag you along. I will bring you from the far north and send you against the mountains of Israel. ³ I will strike your bow from your left hand and make your arrows drop from your right hand. ⁴ On the mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to all kinds of carnivorous birds and to the wild animals. ⁵ You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

⁶ I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in safety in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD. ⁷ I will make my holy name known among my people Israel. I will not let my holy name be profaned anymore. Then the nations will know that I the LORD am the Holy One in Israel. ⁸ It is coming! It will happen, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day I have spoken of. ⁹ Then those who live in the towns of Israel will go out and use the weapons for fuel — the shields and bucklers, the bows and arrows, the war clubs and spears — and they will make fires with them for seven years. ¹⁰ They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, because they will use the weapons for fuel. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord GOD.

¹¹ On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel — the valley of those who travel east of the sea. It will block the path of travelers, because Gog and all his multitude will be buried there. It will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog. ¹² For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land. ¹³ All the people of the land will help with the burial, and it will bring them honor on the day I am glorified, declares the Lord GOD. ¹⁴ They will appoint men to continually search the land and bury any remains left on the ground, in order to cleanse it. After seven months, they will begin the search. ¹⁵ As those who travel through the land survey it, whenever someone sees a human bone, they will set up a marker beside it until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.

¹⁶ A town called Hamonah will also be there. In this way they will cleanse the land. ¹⁷ And you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Speak to every kind of bird and to all the wild animals: "Assemble and come together from all around for the sacrifice I am making for you — a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood. ¹⁸ You will eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of the princes of the earth — the rams, lambs, goats, and bulls — all of them fattened animals from Bashan. ¹⁹ At my sacrifice, which I will prepare for you, you will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk. ²⁰ At my table you will fill yourselves with horses and riders, with mighty men and all kinds of warriors, declares the Lord GOD."

²¹ I will display my glory among the nations, and all the nations will witness my judgment that I execute and my hand that I lay upon them. ²² From that day forward, the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God. ²³ And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile because of their sin — because they were unfaithful to me, I hid my face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword. ²⁴ I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their rebellions, and I hid my face from them. ²⁵ Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy name.

²⁶ They will forget their shame and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me when they lived securely in their land with no one to frighten them. ²⁷ When I have brought them back from the peoples and gathered them out of the lands of their enemies, I will be shown holy through them in the sight of many nations. ²⁸ Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, who sent them into exile among the nations, and who gathered them back to their own land. I will not leave any of them behind. ²⁹ I will no longer hide my face from them, for I will pour out my Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.

¹ In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month — in the fourteenth year after the city fell — on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me and he brought me there. ² In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose south side there was a structure that looked like a city. ³ He brought me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He stood at the gate, holding a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand. ⁴ The man said to me, "Son of man, look carefully and listen closely, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Report everything you see to the house of Israel." ⁵ I saw a wall completely surrounding the outside of the temple. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six long cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handwidth. He measured the thickness of the wall — one rod — and its height — one rod.

⁶ Then he went to the gate that faces east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate — one rod wide — and the other threshold — also one rod wide. ⁷ Each alcove was one rod long and one rod wide, with a space of five cubits between the alcoves. The gate threshold near the gate's inner porch was one rod deep. ⁸ He also measured the inner porch of the gate — one rod. ⁹ Then he measured the porch of the gate — eight cubits — and its jambs — two cubits. The gate porch faced inward. ¹⁰ On each side of the east gate were three alcoves. The three on each side were the same size, and the jambs on either side were the same size.

¹¹ He measured the width of the gate entrance — ten cubits — and the total length of the gateway — thirteen cubits. ¹² In front of each alcove was a ledge one cubit wide on each side. Each alcove was six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other. ¹³ He measured the gateway from the top of the rear wall of one alcove to the top of the opposite one — a width of twenty-five cubits from opening to opening. ¹⁴ He measured the jambs — sixty cubits tall — up to the courtyard all around the gate. ¹⁵ From the front of the entrance gateway to the front of the inner porch was fifty cubits.

¹⁶ The alcoves and their jambs had narrow windows all around the inside of the gateway, and the porticos also had windows all around the inside. Palm trees decorated the jambs. ¹⁷ Then he brought me into the outer court. I saw rooms and a pavement that had been made all around the court. Thirty rooms faced onto the pavement. ¹⁸ The pavement on both sides of the gates was as wide as the gates were long — this was the lower pavement. ¹⁹ Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the front of the inner court — a hundred cubits on the east side and on the north side. ²⁰ The gate of the outer court that faced north — he measured its length and width.

²¹ It had three alcoves on each side, with jambs and porticos of the same measurements as the first gate — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ²² Its windows, porticos, and palm trees were the same dimensions as those of the east gate. You went up seven steps to reach it, and its portico faced you as you approached. ²³ There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was one facing the east gate. He measured the distance from gate to gate — a hundred cubits. ²⁴ Then he led me to the south side, where I saw a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and porticos — they had the same dimensions as the others. ²⁵ The gate and its porticos had windows all around, like the previous windows — fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

²⁶ Seven steps led up to it, and its portico faced the approach, with a palm tree on each side of the jambs. ²⁷ The inner court also had a gate facing south. He measured from that gate to the outer south gate — a hundred cubits. ²⁸ Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate and measured it — it had the same measurements as the others. ²⁹ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos all had the same dimensions, with windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁰ The porticos all around were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.

³¹ Its porticos faced the outer court, and palm trees adorned the jambs. Eight steps led up to it. ³² He brought me to the inner court on the east side and measured the gate — it had the same dimensions as the others. ³³ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos had the same measurements, and it had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁴ Its porticos faced the outer court, with palm trees on both sides of the jambs. Eight steps led up to it. ³⁵ He brought me to the north gate and measured it — it had the same dimensions as the others.

³⁶ Its alcoves, jambs, and porticos were all there, with windows all around. The gate was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. ³⁷ Its jambs faced the outer court, and palm trees were on both sides of them. Eight steps led up to it. ³⁸ A room with a doorway opened onto the gateway porticos, where the burnt offerings were washed. ³⁹ Inside the gateway portico there were two tables on each side, where the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were slaughtered. ⁴⁰ By the outer wall near the north gateway steps were two tables, and on the other side of the porch were two more tables.

⁴¹ So there were four tables inside the gateway and four outside — eight tables in all, on which the sacrifices were slaughtered. ⁴² There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offerings, each one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit high. The instruments used to slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices were laid on these. ⁴³ Double hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside walls, and the flesh of the offerings lay on the tables. ⁴⁴ Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, there were two rooms — one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the east gate facing north. ⁴⁵ He said to me, "The room facing south is for the priests who have charge of the temple.

⁴⁶ The room facing north is for the priests who have charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who are the Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before him." ⁴⁷ He measured the inner court — a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a perfect square. The altar stood in front of the temple. ⁴⁸ He brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the jambs of the portico — five cubits on each side. The gateway was fourteen cubits wide, with shoulders of three cubits on each side. ⁴⁹ The portico was twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, with ten steps leading up to it, and pillars beside the jambs on both sides.

¹ Then he brought me to the main hall and measured the doorposts — six cubits wide on each side — the width of the tabernacle. ² The entrance was ten cubits wide, and its side walls were five cubits on each side. He measured the hall — forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. ³ Then he went into the inner room and measured the doorpost — two cubits. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side of the entrance were seven cubits. ⁴ He then measured the length — twenty cubits — and the width — twenty cubits — in front of the main hall. He said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place." ⁵ He measured the outer wall of the temple — six cubits thick. The side rooms all around the temple were four cubits wide.

⁶ The side rooms were arranged in three stories, one above another, thirty rooms on each level. There were ledges built into the outer wall of the temple all around to serve as supports for the side rooms, so the supports were not embedded in the temple wall. ⁷ The side rooms became wider as they went higher, since the temple was surrounded by a winding passage that narrowed toward the top. The width of the side rooms increased from the lowest level upward, with the middle level being wider than the lowest and the upper level being wider than the middle. ⁸ I saw that the temple had a raised platform all around. The foundation of the side rooms was a full rod — six cubits — high. ⁹ The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side rooms and the inner rooms ¹⁰ was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.

¹¹ The side rooms had doorways opening onto the open area — one doorway facing north and one facing south. The open area was five cubits wide all around. ¹² The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and the building itself was ninety cubits long. ¹³ Then he measured the temple — it was a hundred cubits long. The temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long. ¹⁴ The width of the temple facing east, including the courtyard, was a hundred cubits. ¹⁵ He measured the length of the building on the west side, facing the temple courtyard, including its galleries on both sides — a hundred cubits — along with the inner temple and the porticos of the court.

¹⁶ The doorposts, the narrow windows, and the three-story galleries all around — from the ground to the windows, which were covered — the interior from the ground up to the windows was paneled with wood all around. ¹⁷ The space above the outer doorway leading into the inner room, and the walls all the way around inside and outside, were laid out by measurement. ¹⁸ The wall was decorated with carved cherubim and palm trees alternating — a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces: ¹⁹ a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side and the face of a young lion turned toward the palm tree on the other side. These carvings were all around the interior of the temple. ²⁰ From the floor to above the entrance, the walls were decorated with cherubim and palm trees.

²¹ The doorposts of the main hall were squared, and the front of the sanctuary had the same appearance. ²² The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long. It had corners, and its base and sides were of wood. He said to me, "This is the table that stands before the LORD." ²³ Both the main hall and the sanctuary had double doors. ²⁴ Each door had two folding panels — two leaves for each door. ²⁵ The doors of the main hall were carved with cherubim and palm trees, just like those on the walls. Outside, in front of the portico, there was a wooden overhang.
²⁶ There were narrow windows and palm trees on both sides of the portico, on the side walls of the temple, and on the overhangs.

¹ Then he led me out to the outer court by way of the north and brought me to the rooms that were across from the courtyard and from the outer wall on the north side. ² The building to the north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide. ³ Facing the twenty-cubit inner court and the outer-court pavement, the galleries ran opposite each other at three levels. ⁴ In front of the rooms was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long, with their doorways on the north. ⁵ The upper rooms were narrower, because the galleries took more space from them than from the rooms on the lower and middle floors.

⁶ These upper rooms had no pillars like the pillars in the courts, so they were smaller than the lower and middle rooms, going back from the ground level. ⁷ The outer wall ran parallel to the rooms toward the outer court for fifty cubits. ⁸ while the row of rooms facing the outer court was fifty cubits long, and those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long. ⁹ Below the lower rooms was an entrance on the east side as one approached them from the outer court. ¹⁰ Where the outer court wall began, there were rooms along its south side, facing the temple courtyard and the outer wall.

¹¹ There was a walkway in front of them like the walkway of the rooms on the north. Their length and width were the same, and their exits and arrangements were the same. The south rooms were entered the same way as the north rooms — ¹² from the east, at the front of the passage where the inner wall begins. ¹³ Then he said to me, "The north and south rooms facing the temple courtyard are the holy rooms where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will deposit the most holy offerings — the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings — for the place is holy. ¹⁴ Once the priests have entered, they shall not go out from the holy area into the outer court without first removing the garments in which they minister, for those garments are holy. They shall put on other clothes before approaching the areas open to the people." ¹⁵ When he had finished measuring the inside of the temple area, he led me out through the east gate and measured all around.

¹⁶ He measured the east side with the measuring rod — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁷ He measured the north side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁸ He measured the south side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁹ He turned and measured the west side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ²⁰ He measured the wall on all four sides. It was five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, creating a separation between what was holy and what was common.

¹ Then he led me to the gate — the gate facing east. ² And there was the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of rushing waters, and the land was radiant with his glory. ³ The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and like the vision I had seen by the Chebar River. I fell facedown. ⁴ The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east. ⁵ The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

⁶ I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple, while the man was standing beside me. ⁷ He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet. This is where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will never again defile my holy name — neither they nor their kings — by their prostitution and by the corpses of their kings at their high places. ⁸ When they placed their threshold next to my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only a wall between us, they defiled my holy name by their detestable practices. So I destroyed them in my anger. ⁹ Now let them put away their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever. ¹⁰ You, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so they may be ashamed of their sins. Let them study its design.

¹¹ If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple — its arrangement, its exits and entrances, its entire design, and all its regulations and instructions. Write it down in their presence so they may faithfully follow its entire design and all its decrees. ¹² This is the law of the temple: all the surrounding area on top of the mountain is most holy. This is the law of the temple. ¹³ These are the measurements of the altar in cubits — the cubit being a standard cubit plus a handwidth: the base is one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a rim of one span around the edge. This is the base of the altar. ¹⁴ From the base at ground level up to the lower ledge is two cubits high and one cubit wide. From the smaller ledge up to the larger ledge is four cubits high and one cubit wide. ¹⁵ The altar hearth is four cubits high, with four horns projecting upward from the hearth.

¹⁶ The altar hearth is twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide — a perfect square. ¹⁷ The upper ledge is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, also square, with a rim of half a cubit and a surrounding channel of one cubit. The steps face east." ¹⁸ Then he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the regulations for the altar when it is built, for sacrificing burnt offerings and splashing blood on it. ¹⁹ You are to give to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who come near to minister before me, declares the Lord GOD, a young bull as a sin offering. ²⁰ You shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, the four corners of the upper ledge, and the surrounding rim. In this way you will cleanse it and make atonement for it.

²¹ Take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the designated part of the temple grounds, outside the sanctuary. ²² On the second day offer a male goat without defect as a sin offering. Cleanse the altar as you cleansed it with the bull. ²³ When you have finished the purification, offer a young bull without defect and a ram from the flock without defect. ²⁴ Present them before the LORD, and the priests shall sprinkle salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD. ²⁵ For seven days you shall prepare a goat for a sin offering each day, as well as a young bull and a ram from the flock — all without defect.

²⁶ For seven days they shall purify the altar and consecrate it, and so dedicate it. ²⁷ When these days are over, then from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer on the altar your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings. I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.

¹ Then he brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary facing east, and it was shut. ² The LORD said to me, "This gate is to remain shut. It must not be opened; no one may enter through it. It is to remain shut because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. ³ The prince himself is the only one who may sit in the gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD. He is to enter by way of the portico of the gateway and go out the same way." ⁴ Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple, and I fell facedown. ⁵ The LORD said to me, "Son of man, pay close attention and look carefully and listen closely to everything I tell you concerning all the regulations and instructions regarding the temple of the LORD. Pay close attention to the entrance of the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary.

⁶ Say to the rebellious house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough of your detestable practices, house of Israel! ⁷ When you brought in foreigners — uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in body — to be in my sanctuary, you desecrated it. While you were offering me food, fat, and blood, they broke my covenant with all your detestable practices. ⁸ Instead of carrying out your duty regarding my holy things, you appointed them to keep charge of my sanctuary for you. ⁹ This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and body, shall enter my sanctuary — not even the foreigners who live among the Israelites. ¹⁰ As for the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, straying after their idols, they must bear the consequences of their sin.

¹¹ They may serve in my sanctuary as gatekeepers and as workers in the temple. They may slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices for the people and stand before the people to serve them. ¹² But because they served the people before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I swore against them with an uplifted hand, declares the Lord GOD, and they must bear the consequences of their sin. ¹³ They shall not approach me to serve as priests or come near any of my holy things or my most holy offerings. They must bear their shame and the consequences of the detestable things they have done. ¹⁴ Yet I will appoint them to guard the temple and carry out all its maintenance and all the work that is to be done in it. ¹⁵ But the Levitical priests, who are descendants of Zadok and who guarded my sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from me, shall come near to minister before me. They shall stand in my presence to offer me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.

¹⁶ They are the ones who shall enter my sanctuary and come near to my table to minister before me. They shall keep my charge. ¹⁷ When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments. They shall wear no wool while ministering at the gates of the inner court or inside it. ¹⁸ They shall wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They shall not wear anything that causes sweat. ¹⁹ When they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall take off the garments in which they were ministering and leave them in the holy rooms. Then they shall put on other clothes so they do not consecrate the people by means of their garments. ²⁰ They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but shall keep their hair trimmed.

²¹ No priest shall drink wine before entering the inner court. ²² They shall not marry widows or divorced women; they may only marry virgins from the Israelite community or widows of priests. ²³ They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean. ²⁴ When there is a dispute, they shall serve as judges and decide it according to my ordinances. They shall keep my laws and my statutes regarding all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy. ²⁵ A priest shall not make himself ceremonially unclean by going near a dead person. However, he may defile himself for a father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or an unmarried sister.

²⁶ After a priest is cleansed, he must wait seven more days. ²⁷ On the day he enters the inner court of the sanctuary to minister there, he shall offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Lord GOD. ²⁸ The priests shall have no land of their own in Israel — I am their inheritance. You are not to give them any property in Israel; I am their possession. ²⁹ They shall eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings. Everything devoted to God in Israel will belong to them. ³⁰ The first of all the firstfruits and all the special contributions of every kind shall belong to the priests. You shall also give the priests the first portion of your ground grain, so that a blessing may rest on your household.
³¹ The priests shall not eat anything — whether bird or animal — that has died naturally or been torn by wild animals.

¹ "When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you shall set apart a sacred portion of the land for the LORD.
